job_ca709075-e1a2-46a3-88b3-672ffd94443d.promptFull:
Create a 22-second high-energy experimental cinematic film built around perfect visual match cuts.

The entire video feels like one piece of visual music.
Fast, precise, elegant editing.
Every new shot must emerge from the shape, motion, texture or direction of the previous shot.

Premium fashion-film meets surreal visual art.
Photorealistic, tactile, bold, modern.
No text, no logos, no subtitles.

SHOT 1 — 0:00–0:02
EXTREME MACRO.
A human eye in almost complete darkness suddenly opens.
The iris is intensely detailed, wet, reflective, deep cobalt blue.
A single heartbeat.
The camera rapidly pushes straight into the pupil.

MATCH CUT:

SHOT 2 — 0:02–0:04
The black pupil becomes a total solar eclipse in a gigantic pale sky.
The glowing corona pulses exactly on the beat.
Camera accelerates violently toward the center of the eclipse.

MATCH CUT:

SHOT 3 — 0:04–0:06
The eclipse becomes the circular entrance of a futuristic concrete tunnel.
Camera rockets through the tunnel at extreme speed, inches above the ground.
Lights streak overhead.
Sharp rushing wind and rhythmic metallic impacts.

WHIP TRANSITION:

SHOT 4 — 0:06–0:08
A spinning black vinyl record fills the frame.
The rotation continues with exactly the same direction and speed as the tunnel movement.
A chrome needle drops onto the record precisely on the beat.
CRACK.
The soundtrack suddenly gains an aggressive electronic bass pulse.

MACRO MATCH CUT:

SHOT 5 — 0:08–0:10
The microscopic grooves of the vinyl become enormous aerial ridges of black desert sand.
Camera now flies at impossible speed just above the dunes.
Wind throws particles directly toward the lens.

SHOT 6 — 0:10–0:12.5
One dune rises upward and seamlessly becomes the flowing folds of a gigantic crimson couture dress.

Reveal an adult female dancer alone inside an enormous brutalist white room.
She spins once, violently and beautifully.
The camera performs a fast 270-degree orbit around her.
Fabric explodes outward with realistic weight and physics.

ON THE MUSICAL HIT:

SHOT 7 — 0:12.5–0:14.5
The crimson fabric fills the entire frame and instantly becomes a gigantic red ocean wave.
Camera is now inside the barrel of the wave, traveling forward at extreme speed.
Detailed translucent water, droplets on lens, deep physical impact.

SHOT 8 — 0:14.5–0:16.5
At the moment the wave crashes, the water freezes into transparent glass.

TIME SLOWS FOR HALF A SECOND.

The entire glass wave shatters toward camera.

Then immediate speed ramp.

Thousands of floating shards shoot past the lens in perfect synchronization with the music.

SHOT 9 — 0:16.5–0:19
The flying glass fragments transform mid-motion into thousands of city lights.

Reveal:
we are flying backward at enormous speed above a vast futuristic city at night.

Camera continues pulling farther and farther away.
The entire city begins becoming smaller.

SHOT 10 — 0:19–0:22
The glowing city is revealed to be nothing more than a reflection inside the pupil of the SAME HUMAN EYE from the opening shot.

Extreme macro again.

The camera finishes pulling back.

One final heartbeat.

The eye closes.

CUT TO BLACK exactly on the beat.

AUDIO:
Create one continuous original electronic cinematic soundtrack that drives every edit.
Strong sub-bass pulse, heartbeat motif, sharp percussive impacts, vinyl needle crack, rushing tunnel air, desert wind, fabric movement, ocean impact, breaking glass and distant city ambience.
Every major visual transition must happen precisely on a musical hit.
Sound effects must change naturally with each environment while the underlying rhythm remains continuous.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
aggressive editorial pacing
rapid match cuts
whip pans
crash zooms
speed ramps
macro cinematography
extreme scale changes
strong visual geometry
realistic motion blur
physical camera movement
high-end commercial cinematography
controlled deep blacks
crimson red accents
chrome reflections
tactile textures
natural photographic detail
dramatic contrast
subtle film grain

Maintain clear visual readability despite the fast pacing.
Do not create random unrelated montage.
Each transformation must visually motivate the next shot.
No text.
No typography.
No logos.
No watermark.

3df64f8c-969b-42b0-b83d-71a680503e52.promptFull: [STYLE + CAMERA + ATMOSPHERE] Raw handheld smartphone video, one unbroken continuous take for the full 30 seconds. Vertical 9:16. Shot from the front passenger seat of another car traveling alongside a weathered American pickup on a multi-lane American highway in daylight. The passenger is holding the phone inside the open side window, forearms braced against the door. Hard organic shake from road seams, roll and yaw on bumps, accidental tilt, slight windshield dirt visible when the phone turns inward, grain, crushed shadows, imperfect exposure, autofocus hunting then locking, wind slap and traffic roar on the mic. The operator is a person holding a phone, trying to understand something outrageous happening beside them. Real digital zoom only: one brief, modest, clumsy thumb pinch-zoom at the beginning, slight overshoot, soft compression while zooming, then a late snap to sharp. Most of the take stays medium-wide so the truck, people, animal, moving roadway and adjacent space remain readable together. Framing changes primarily through relative vehicle movement and the passenger physically turning the phone. The camera reacts late. No cinematic coverage, no extreme close-ups, no cuts or hidden transitions. Lived-in documentary phone footage. Every beat follows the previous one in order. [CHARACTER + VEHICLE + PROP CONTINUITY] Establish the following cast, vehicles and props from the first frame and preserve their appearance and positions throughout the take. Same weathered maroon American pickup, same matte bed liner, same crooked JUST MARRIED sign attached to the rear bumper, same modest single-axle trailer attached by a visible tow hitch. The bride is a heavyset adult American woman with a deep tan, platinum-blonde teased hair, a short veil, hoop earrings, a slightly rumpled white strapless wedding dress and brown cowboy boots. She is loud, affectionate and unselfconscious. The groom is a broad, heavyset adult American man with a thick reddish beard, sunburned shoulders, tattoos, a white ribbed tank top, black suit trousers and worn work boots. He holds a beer can. Keep the same adult faces, bodies and wardrobe throughout. One stocky pink pig with a small black bow tie stands in the bed near their boots. It behaves like an ordinary food-motivated pig, never like a person. One bouquet of pale flowers and green stems. A shallow disposable aluminum tray with a few bread rolls rests precariously on the bed rail nearest the filming car. The couple's old vinyl bench is fixed against the cab, facing the open tailgate. Two adult wedding guests sit in folding chairs secured to the trailer: a woman in pink sunglasses and a man in a short-sleeved patterned shirt. Maintain these identities, counts and object locations. [PLACE] Multi-lane American highway under harsh midday sunlight. The pickup and filming car are already moving side by side at matched road speed at second 0. The filming car is in the lane immediately to the pickup's left, slightly behind the pickup cab, looking diagonally through its passenger-side window into the open bed. The trailer follows directly behind the pickup. Nearby traffic keeps moving with them. Both vehicles remain in uninterrupted forward motion for the entire 30 seconds. No braking, stopping, pulling over or restarting. Lane markings continuously stream backward, roadside trees and guardrails pass, wheels rotate, the short veil and loose clothing pull in the wind. The filming car gains only a few meters gradually over the full take. The operator turns the phone progressively backward to maintain sight of the bed. This is continuous road motion, not a static tableau with a moving background. The groom starts near the open tailgate, the bride immediately beside him. A transverse pavement seam crosses the roadway ahead and later causes a single visible jolt. The driver of the pickup stays in the cab and maintains speed. All physical action remains localized and readable. [TIMELINE — ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE, HANDHELD + DIGITAL ZOOM ONLY] 0.0–4.0s: [HOOK — ROLLING WEDDING ALREADY IN PROGRESS] Phone already rolling. LEFT foreground: a narrow edge of the filming car's open passenger window. CENTER/RIGHT: the pickup moving beside us. The bride and groom are already kissing in the open bed, swaying with the road. His beer can remains in one hand; her bouquet hangs low in the other. The short veil flutters hard. The crooked JUST MARRIED sign and part of the following trailer establish the homemade wedding procession. Guests raise their drinks. The pig is already visible at the couple's feet, sniffing the low bouquet. A small, awkward digital zoom helps the operator recognize the scene, then settles into a medium-wide view. Behind the phone, an amused adult American male voice says, "Bro... is that a wedding?" Wind partly masks the end of the sentence. The road never stops moving. 4.0–8.0s: [PIG GRABS BOUQUET — CAUSE] The pig bites the flowers and pulls downward. The bride breaks the kiss and tugs back, still gripping the stems. The groom briefly leans toward the kiss she has left, then notices and bends to help. His elbow visibly strikes the shallow aluminum tray on the near bed rail. The tray tips toward the filming car's side, dumping several bread rolls onto the moving road. Airflow catches the now-light empty tray and lifts it off the rail. Keep elbow contact, tipping, falling bread and wind catching the tray in that causal order. The pig keeps its grip on the flowers. The phone remains wide enough to see the accident develop without a close-up. 8.0–12.0s: [THE CHAOS REACHES THE CAMERA] The empty aluminum tray tumbles through the short gap between the vehicles and clips the EXTERIOR passenger-side window pillar of the filming car with a sharp hollow metallic slap. It deflects backward and out of view, remaining outside the cabin. The passenger recoils away from the open window. The phone pitches briefly toward the dashboard and the edge of the windshield; the moving highway remains visible in the upper part of the image. No blackout or hidden cut. The passenger blurts, "Oh shit!" The offscreen driver snaps, "Keep your arm inside!" Engine and wind continue without interruption. The filming car holds its lane. The operator immediately tries to find the pickup again. 12.0–18.0s: [ROAD JOLT — GROOM LOSES HIS FOOTING] The phone swings back to the pickup late. The groom has straightened and turned toward the filming car, raising his free hand in apology. The truck's rear wheels cross the visible transverse pavement seam; the bed jolts once. His boot slips off the open tailgate. One leg drops outside, his torso stays inside the bed, and his free hand immediately grabs the near bed rail. The bride catches a fistful of the back of his tank top. His beer can falls from his other hand, hits the asphalt and bounces backward relative to the moving vehicles. The passenger exclaims, "Whoa, whoa, WHOA!" His voice now sounds genuinely alarmed. Maintain medium-wide framing so the open tailgate, hanging leg, gripping hand, bride's hold and streaming roadway are readable together. The pickup keeps moving at the same speed. 18.0–24.0s: [MESSY RECOVERY WHILE STILL MOVING] The groom plants his lowered boot on the rear bumper, pushes upward, gets one knee back onto the open tailgate and hauls himself into the bed while the bride pulls on his tank top. The shirt stretches visibly but remains on his body. Each support point bears real weight. No floating, flipping or miraculous jump. They stumble the short distance back into the fixed vinyl bench and collapse onto it together. The bride still holds a few stripped bouquet stems; the pig has the flower heads and keeps chewing near their boots. On the trailer, the woman in pink sunglasses half-rises in alarm, grips her chair and sits again. A nearby horn sounds. The phone continues trembling, without zooming in. 24.0–30.0s: [BACK TO THE KISS — CLOSE] Seated on the bench, the groom gives the filming passenger a sheepish apologetic wave, his tank top hanging badly stretched. The bride gives the back of his head a brief exasperated tap, takes his beard gently in one hand, pulls him toward her and resumes the kiss. The pig stays below them, calmly chewing the stolen flowers. One guest on the trailer raises a drink again. The operator exhales, then says with disbelieving laughter, "They're still kissing. Bro..." The filming car has gradually gained a few meters. The passenger turns the phone backward to keep the moving pickup in view. The framing gets a little crooked and starts losing the trailer. End while the pickup is still rolling beside and slightly behind us: couple kissing, pig chewing flowers, short veil blowing, road streaming past. Phone still trembling. One continuous take from rolling kiss to pig to airborne tray to near fall to recovery to rolling kiss. [STYLE & QUALITY BOOSTERS] Single continuous 30-second raw handheld phone take, vertical 9:16. Modest digital pinch-zoom only at the beginning. Predominantly medium-wide witness framing. Strict character, vehicle and prop continuity. Causal order only: kiss already happening on moving pickup → pig grabs low bouquet → groom bends and knocks tray → wind carries empty tray into filming car's exterior pillar → filmer recoils and recovers framing → pavement seam jolts pickup → groom slips and catches rail → bride helps him climb back → couple resumes kissing while pig keeps chewing. Continuous vehicle motion from first frame to last. Stable lane geography and believable relative speeds. Real weight, wind-driven lightweight aluminum, bread and can falling onto asphalt then receding behind moving vehicles, boot contact with bumper, fabric tension, road vibration and imperfect phone autofocus. No giant jumps, animal tricks or supernatural events. The spectacle comes from outrageous human choices filmed as a plausible roadside encounter. Natural American voices from inside the filming car, short spontaneous reactions rather than narration. Do not force polished speech or interrupt the action for dialogue. Traffic and wind may partially obscure words. No music, subtitles, graphics, slow motion, stabilized camera or cinematic color grade. Maintain damage and prop continuity: tray and can do not return; bouquet remains eaten; tank top remains stretched.

job_9fcbac35-7b39-4c97-be57-b391c19c8206.promptFull:
Create a 24-second surreal high-fashion cinematic film titled:

GRAVITY FORGOT THE ROOM

The entire film takes place inside the same monumental luxury banquet hall.

The room is long, symmetrical and dramatic:
dark polished stone floor,
towering windows,
cream walls,
one impossibly long white dinner table,
silver cutlery,
crystal glasses,
deep red wine,
white flowers,
hundreds of candles.

Twenty elegantly dressed adult guests sit around the table.

The visual language is:
high-fashion editorial,
surreal performance art,
precise choreography,
fast cinematic montage,
luxurious but strange,
photorealistic,
bold camera movement.

At first everything feels completely normal.

Then gravity begins to fail.

SHOT 1 — 0:00–0:02.5

Perfect symmetrical ultra-wide shot.

All guests sit silently at the enormous table.

Nobody moves.

Only candle flames flicker.

A waiter enters from the far end carrying a silver tray.

Very quiet room tone.
Tiny sounds of crystal and cutlery.

The camera slowly pushes forward.

SHOT 2 — 0:02.5–0:04.5

EXTREME MACRO.

A single drop of red wine falls from a crystal glass.

But instead of falling downward...

it stops in mid-air.

Silence.

The wine droplet slowly rises.

A deep bass tone begins.

SHOT 3 — 0:04.5–0:06.5

FAST SIDE TRACKING SHOT along the entire banquet table.

One object after another begins floating upward:

a fork,
a napkin,
a strawberry,
a rose petal,
a crystal glass,
then dozens of objects.

The guests remain perfectly calm.

Their eyes follow the objects upward.

Each floating object creates a precise musical click or note.

The soundtrack begins building rhythmically.

SHOT 4 — 0:06.5–0:08.5

OVERHEAD SHOT.

Gravity suddenly rotates 90 degrees.

Everything slides violently sideways across the table.

Plates,
fruit,
flowers,
cutlery,
candles.

The guests grab the table.

The camera rotates with gravity so that the wall becomes the floor.

Fast physical movement.
Realistic inertia.
Nothing should feel weightless or random.

SHOT 5 — 0:08.5–0:10.5

SMASH CUT.

A woman in an elegant black evening dress is now walking calmly along the SIDE WALL as if it were the floor.

Her long dress hangs naturally toward the new direction of gravity.

Camera performs a rapid vertical crane move beside her.

Behind her, chairs and glasses slowly fall sideways.

She never reacts.

Editorial confidence.

SHOT 6 — 0:10.5–0:12.5

Gravity disappears completely.

ZERO GRAVITY.

Rapid macro montage synchronized to percussion:

— red wine forms a perfect floating sphere
— silver cutlery rotates slowly
— a white rose explodes into individual petals
— a candle flame stretches into an impossible glowing shape
— pearls from a necklace drift through the air
— water droplets collide and merge

Fast rhythmic cutting.

Highly detailed textures.

SHOT 7 — 0:12.5–0:15

The music suddenly accelerates.

A male guest pushes gently away from his chair.

He flies horizontally above the banquet table.

Camera flies beside him at matching speed.

He passes through hundreds of floating objects.

A glass rotates inches from camera.
A strawberry passes his face.
A ribbon of red wine moves like fabric through the air.

The camera rolls 180 degrees while tracking him.

SHOT 8 — 0:15–0:17.5

THE ENTIRE ROOM ERUPTS INTO CHOREOGRAPHY.

Fast cuts:

A woman spins through floating flowers.

Two guests pass each other upside-down.

A waiter calmly pours wine even though both waiter and bottle are floating.

A chandelier rotates slowly through the background.

A dinner plate flies toward camera and narrowly misses the lens.

Camera whip pans between actions.

Everything moves in rhythm with the music.

SHOT 9 — 0:17.5–0:20.5

The soundtrack reaches maximum intensity.

Gravity begins switching direction rapidly on every beat.

DOWN.

LEFT.

UP.

RIGHT.

Each musical hit completely changes the direction of gravity.

Guests and objects react physically to each shift.

Use extremely fast cuts between:

wide shot,
macro shot,
POV,
top-down,
handheld close-up,
fast dolly shot.

The banquet hall remains visually consistent throughout.

SHOT 10 — 0:20.5–0:22.5

Suddenly—

TOTAL SILENCE.

Gravity returns to normal.

Everything crashes downward simultaneously.

But instead of chaos...

CUT precisely before impact.

SHOT 11 — 0:22.5–0:24

Same perfectly symmetrical composition as the opening shot.

Everything is back in its original position.

Perfect table.
Perfect flowers.
Perfect guests.

Nobody moves.

The waiter calmly places the silver tray onto the table.

Tiny crystal sound.

One guest looks directly into camera.

A single red wine droplet rises upward behind them.

CUT TO BLACK.

AUDIO DIRECTION:

Crystal taps become percussion.
Cutlery becomes metallic rhythm.
Wine glasses become musical tones.
Chair movement becomes bass.
Breathing and fabric movement become texture.

As gravity becomes increasingly unstable, the music becomes faster and more complex.

Every gravity shift must happen exactly on a strong musical beat.

Use dramatic silence immediately before the final reset.

VISUAL DIRECTION:

luxury fashion campaign
surreal European cinema
editorial photography
monumental architecture
fast precise cutting
extreme macro cinematography
high-speed camera movement
whip pans
camera rolls
crash zooms
overhead compositions
symmetry
realistic human motion
realistic object physics
realistic liquid simulation
detailed glass reflections
natural skin texture
beautiful fabric physics
volumetric candlelight
cinematic shadows
subtle film grain

IMPORTANT:

The banquet hall, table and guests must remain visually coherent between shots.

Gravity changes must affect clothing, hair, liquids and loose objects physically and consistently.

Do not make the floating objects random or chaotic.

The movement must feel deliberately choreographed.

No text.
No logos.
No subtitles.
No watermark.

job_ff94f180-0a2f-4f2b-acb2-bda8352fa9d9.promptFull:
Create a 24-second ultra-stylized experimental underground music film.

TITLE / CONCEPT:
HARD BOUNCE

One fluorescent orange ball drives the entire edit.

Every impact, bounce, spin or circular motion creates the next shot.

The film becomes progressively faster, stranger and more visually aggressive.

The ORANGE CIRCLE is the recurring graphic motif:
basketball,
wheel,
vinyl record,
speaker,
washing-machine window,
human eye,
tunnel light,
moon,
then basketball again.

Every transition must be visually motivated by:
SHAPE,
MOTION,
DIRECTION,
or IMPACT.

This is NOT a story.
This is visual rhythm.

Dark, raw, underground, tactile, energetic.
Photorealistic but highly art-directed.

No text.
No logos.
No subtitles.

--------------------------------
SHOT 1 — 0:00–0:02
--------------------------------

TOTAL BLACK.

A fluorescent orange basketball drops from above into a single hard spotlight.

Concrete floor.

BOOM.

One massive dry impact.

On the first bounce, camera drops violently with the ball.

Second bounce:

BOOM.

HARD CUT EXACTLY ON IMPACT.

--------------------------------
SHOT 2 — 0:02–0:04
--------------------------------

Nighttime underground basketball court.

Wet black asphalt.
Chain-link fencing.
Sodium-vapor lights.
Steam in the distance.

EXTREME LOW FISHEYE CAMERA only centimeters above the floor.

A player in black sneakers dribbles the orange ball directly toward camera.

BOOM.
BOOM.
BOOM.

Each bounce becomes part of the beat.

On the final bounce, the ball completely fills frame.

MATCH CUT.

--------------------------------
SHOT 3 — 0:04–0:05.7
--------------------------------

The orange circle becomes the glowing hub of a motorcycle wheel.

Camera mounted inches beside the spinning wheel.

The motorcycle races through a wet concrete tunnel.

Reflections streak across the road.

Extreme speed.
Strong parallax.
Realistic vibration.

The wheel spins faster.

MATCH CUT ON ROTATION.

--------------------------------
SHOT 4 — 0:05.7–0:07.3
--------------------------------

A BLACK VINYL RECORD spins at exactly the same speed.

Orange center label.

Extreme macro.

Needle violently drops.

CRACK.

Bass enters.

Rapid macro details:
grooves,
dust,
needle vibration,
chrome reflections.

Camera dives INTO the spinning grooves.

--------------------------------
SHOT 5 — 0:07.3–0:09
--------------------------------

The vinyl grooves become curved concrete lines inside a brutalist skate bowl.

A skateboarder drops in at extreme speed.

Wide fisheye lens.

Camera races backward directly in front of the skateboard.

Wheels scream across concrete.

Skater launches over camera.

The underside of the board wipes the entire frame.

WHIP TRANSITION.

--------------------------------
SHOT 6 — 0:09–0:10.7
--------------------------------

Underground rave.

Almost total darkness.

Hard white strobe.

Bodies appear only for fractions of a second.

Sweat.
Chrome jewelry.
Black clothing.
Condensation.
Hands in the air.

In the center:

a giant circular orange speaker cone pulses.

Every bass hit physically moves the cone.

PUSH IN violently on the speaker.

BOOM.

BOOM.

BOOM.

On the third hit—

camera passes through it.

--------------------------------
SHOT 7 — 0:10.7–0:12.3
--------------------------------

Inside a fluorescent laundromat at 2AM.

Perfect symmetrical composition.

Rows of washing machines.

All machine windows are black...

except ONE glowing orange circular door.

Camera crash-zooms toward it.

Inside, orange fabric spins violently.

SPINNING MOTION MATCH CUT.

--------------------------------
SHOT 8 — 0:12.3–0:14
--------------------------------

EXTREME MACRO HUMAN EYE.

The orange washing-machine circle becomes a vivid amber iris.

Natural skin.
Tiny eyelashes.
Wet eye reflections.

The pupil rapidly contracts.

Reflected inside the pupil:

a subway train approaches.

Camera pushes directly through the pupil.

--------------------------------
SHOT 9 — 0:14–0:16
--------------------------------

SUBWAY PLATFORM.

Train blasts past camera at enormous speed.

Handheld.
Harsh fluorescent light.
Wind hits clothing and newspapers.

Very fast cuts:

train wheel —
shoe hitting platform —
door slamming —
hand grabbing metal rail —
orange emergency light —
eyes —
moving tunnel lights.

Each shot lasts only fractions of a second.

CLACK.
CLACK.
CLACK.
CLACK.

The rhythm accelerates.

--------------------------------
SHOT 10 — 0:16–0:18
--------------------------------

CAMERA IS NOW ATTACHED TO THE FRONT OF THE TRAIN.

We rocket through a black subway tunnel.

Circular tunnel lights flash directly toward camera.

Each light appears for one frame:

WHITE.
BLACK.
ORANGE.
BLACK.
WHITE.
BLACK.

Speed increases impossibly.

Then the final tunnel light becomes enormous.

MATCH CUT.

--------------------------------
SHOT 11 — 0:18–0:20
--------------------------------

The circle is now the FULL MOON.

Huge orange moon above brutalist apartment towers.

Camera drops vertically from the moon toward the city at extreme speed.

Down past rooftops,
balconies,
neon,
fire escapes,
streetlights.

FPV dive.

At street level—

someone throws the orange basketball upward directly toward camera.

--------------------------------
SHOT 12 — 0:20–0:22
--------------------------------

BALL FLIES PAST CAMERA.

ULTRA-FAST RHYTHMIC MONTAGE.

0.2–0.4 second fragments:

basketball bounce

motorcycle wheel

vinyl needle

skateboard landing

speaker pumping

washing machine spinning

eye blinking

subway wheel

tunnel light

moon

ball

Every circular image perfectly aligned in the center of frame.

Faster.

Faster.

Faster.

The soundtrack becomes a brutal synchronized audiovisual crescendo.

--------------------------------
SHOT 13 — 0:22–0:24
--------------------------------

Suddenly:

SILENCE.

Back to the exact dark concrete room from the opening.

The fluorescent orange ball drops into frame.

But this time—

a hand catches it ONE CENTIMETER before it hits the ground.

No impact.

Absolute silence.

Hold.

The fingers slowly release the ball.

floating raindrops,

a frozen scarf,
water hanging above a fountain,
a newspaper stopped mid-turn.

Everything else still moves normally.

SHOT 5 — 0:07.2–0:09.3

a dancer spinning,

**Prompt EN — safer cinematic rooftop run to emotional reunion**

**Brief:**
A cinematic action-drama sequence that begins with an urgent rooftop run and ends in a deeply emotional reunion at home.

**Subject:**
A determined man in his early 30s moves quickly across the rooftops of a dense American city at dusk. He is out of breath, focused, and clearly trying to get home in time. Ahead, one apartment balcony glows with warm golden light. Inside, his wife stands in a beautiful, peaceful family kitchen, surrounded by soft evening light and signs of a happy home.

**Action:**
He sprints across the rooftops with controlled urgency, clears narrow gaps, vaults low walls, ducks under pipes and antennas, and keeps moving without hesitation. He sees the glowing balcony ahead and gathers himself for one final leap. He lands safely on the balcony, pushes the already open glass door wider, and steps inside, breathless. The tension leaves his body immediately. He walks straight to his wife, takes her into his arms, and they share a relieved, emotional kiss. The home around them feels warm, calm, and complete.

**Camera:**
Begin with a fast handheld tracking shot close behind him on the rooftops.
Shift into a side-profile tracking shot as he clears the first gap.
Drop briefly to a low foot-level shot for speed and texture.
Rise into a tight moving close-up as he sees the glowing balcony.
Follow his final leap in one smooth forward move.
Pass with him onto the balcony and through the open doorway in one continuous motion.
Once inside, the camera stabilizes into a smooth, intimate dolly-in.
End on a close three-quarter shot of the embrace and kiss, then a gentle pull-back revealing the warm family space.

**Style:**
Big-screen action drama, photorealistic, grounded and emotional, elegant contrast between cool blue rooftops and warm golden interior light, cinematic motion blur, premium color grade, natural lens breathing, sincere emotional payoff.

**Constraints:**
Keep all movement physical, clean, and believable.
No injuries, no shattered glass, no fight, no weapons, no visible pursuit.
The tone should shift from urgency to tenderness in a seamless cinematic way.
The final moment should feel warm, human, and emotionally real.

Photorealistic, high-contrast, dramatic “blockbuster” lighting.

Shot 1 – 0–4s: Rooftop chase
Exterior, early morning. Vertical shot of a generic action hero sprinting across a city rooftop, wearing casual clothes with a light tactical vibe (no specific franchise, no logos). The camera is in front of the hero, running backwards, very close to their face, cinema-style. Wind in their hair, serious expression, city skyline behind in soft focus. The motion is smooth and dynamic, like a movie trailer.

Dialogue (Shot 1)
The hero, slightly out of breath, mutters to themselves:
“Okay… no pressure… totally under control…”

Hard cut to a side angle: the hero charges towards what looks like the edge of the rooftop. The camera moves with them in profile. The shot is still framed and graded like a serious action scene, but the gap is obviously ridiculous.

“This is just like those movies… please don’t trip now…”

On the laptop screen we see generic, blurred silhouettes of people on a call (no identifiable faces).

Dialogue (Shot 3)
The hero, suddenly very polite, says:
“Hi everyone, sorry I’m late… little… parkour situation.”

On-screen text
At the bottom of the frame between 10 and 12 seconds, add clean white text:
TURN YOUR DAY INTO A MOVIE
Simple sans-serif font, high contrast, sharp and stable.

Generate synchronized audio:
- Big, dramatic trailer-style percussion and pulses in Shots 1 and 2, matching the running and the jump.
- Subtle city ambience under the music on the rooftop (distant traffic, wind).
- A heavy “whoosh” and impact sound as the hero lands in Shot 3.
- As soon as they deliver the punchline, the music drops into a light, cheeky sting, as if the trailer suddenly became a comedy.
No additional voiceover besides the hero’s lines.

Constraints
Keep the hero generic and non-identifiable: no specific actor likeness, no real brand logos.
Do not show real software UI or a recognisable logo on the laptop, just a generic video call layout with blurred silhouettes.
Avoid excessive camera shake; the energy should come from motion, framing and sound, not from random jitter.

TIMELINE & CAMERA (12s total)
0–1s — ESTABLISH: Wide drone/crane shot of rooftops; the agent in black tactical clothing sprints toward camera. Wind, distant siren, low synth pulse.
1–3s — CHASE PUSH: Gimbal handheld runs parallel; quick whip-pan as the agent vaults an AC unit. Footsteps, breath, cloth rustle, metal clank.
3–5s — GAP JUMP: Slow-mo 0.5 s over a roof gap; camera arcs past the agent mid-air. Whoosh, heartbeat thump, rain droplets catch light.
5–7s — GRAPPLE: He fires/throws a compact line that hooks a ledge. Tight insert on magnetic hook. Rope swish, metallic click; score rises with ticking percussion.
7–9s — SWING & DROP: Tracking shot as he swings across and drops to a lower roof beside glowing billboards; helicopter searchlight sweeps past. Rotor wash, city ambience below.
9–11s — LAND & SIGNAL: He lands, shoulder-roll, taps an earpiece and flashes a small data drive. Radio voice (EN, urgent, clean): “You’re clear. Extraction in ten seconds.” Beep.
11–12s — EXIT & HIT: He darts toward a stairwell; behind him a contained secondary blast pops from an empty HVAC unit—bright flash, rolling smoke, shockwave dust. Score hits a final BRAAM; quick fade to black.

AUDIO DIRECTION
- Music: high-tempo hybrid score (percussion + synth pulses), builds steadily, final sting at 11.5s.
- SFX: footsteps, fabric swishes, wind, siren far, hook click, rope whoosh, rotor wash, small controlled explosion (no debris hitting camera).
- Dialogue: one short radio line at 10.2–10.8 s (see above). Keep intelligible, light comms static.

No recognizable faces of real people, no brand names, no copyrighted logos, no weapons fire, no gore, no text overlays, no watermark.

His curly hair is slightly messy, giving him a soft, boyish charm, and his clothing is relaxed: a crewneck sweater and dark jeans. job_dc38e25d-2954-4344-bcfb-414e91a4cf89.promptFull:
Bella sits at a long table draped in a red-and-white checkered tablecloth, a paper plate of half-eaten pasta forgotten in front of her. Her hair is pulled back loosely, wisps framing her face, cheeks flushed from laughter—or maybe from the glass of soda she swears was spiked. She’s wearing a soft cream sweater tucked into a skirt, simple yet graceful, and there’s a faint tomato sauce stain near her sleeve that she hasn’t noticed. Her hands move when she talks, animated and expressive, though her voice is quiet. She’s looking toward Luis across the room, pretending not to, smiling at something he said to someone else. There’s light in her eyes that betrays her—hopeful, curious, maybe even nervous.

Alex:
Alex stands near the food table, armed with tongs and a no-nonsense expression as she refills trays of garlic bread like a general leading her troops. Her hair is tucked behind her ears, her sleeves rolled up, her posture straight. She keeps the chaos organized, directing people to “just grab a plate and move down the line.” But there’s humor in her firmness—every few minutes she breaks into laughter, especially when Jason starts impersonating the club sponsor behind her. She’s wearing a fitted denim jacket over a black turtleneck, gold hoops catching the overhead light when she turns. Alex radiates confidence—the kind of presence that keeps the night from spinning too far out of control.

Jason:
Jason’s sitting backwards on a chair, spinning a plastic fork between his fingers. His curly hair falls into his eyes, and there’s a smudge of marinara sauce near his collar that he either hasn’t noticed or doesn’t care about. He’s talking to a group of students, gesturing wildly, making them all laugh. At one point, he lifts his fork and shouts in mock Italian, “Mangia, mangia!” and the room bursts into laughter. Between jokes, though, his eyes wander to Bella, watching her in the pauses. He sketches her on a napkin when no one’s looking, shading in the soft angle of her jaw with the back of his pen. There’s a restlessness to him, a spark that keeps the whole group alive.

Paul:
Paul leans against the counter near the espresso machine, the hum of conversation swirling around him but not quite touching him. He’s dressed neatly, as always—crisp white button-up, sleeves rolled halfway, a subtle watch glinting under the lights. There’s a composure to him that borders on cool detachment, but when Bella glances over, he’s already looking at her. For a brief second, his face softens—a flicker of the boy she once knew—but then he’s back to his stoic self, sipping from a tiny cup of espresso like he’s in some black-and-white film. He doesn’t say much, but people drift toward him anyway, drawn to his quiet gravity. He looks like he belongs and yet doesn’t—half in the room, half in his own thoughts.

Luis:
Luis is at the center of the laughter, behind the counter helping serve slices of tiramisu, sleeves rolled up, curls a little messy from the heat of the kitchen. He’s wearing a plain dark green sweater that brings out the warmth of his skin and the brightness in his eyes. Every time he laughs—which he does often—it’s from deep in his chest, unguarded and infectious. When Bella approaches to grab dessert, he catches her eye and holds it just a second too long. “You like coffee in your tiramisu, right?” he asks softly, like it’s an inside joke. She nods, heart racing, pretending to look at the dessert instead of him. When he hands her the plate, his fingers brush hers—by accident or maybe not. The air between them stills for a moment before the chatter fills it back in.

The Room Around Them:
The fluorescent lights hum softly above a sea of mismatched decorations—Italian flags, construction paper cutouts of leaning towers, and string lights that twinkle unevenly. The tables are cluttered with plastic cups, spilled marinara, and half-torn breadsticks. Someone’s phone plays “Mambo Italiano” too loud. There’s a warmth that feels nostalgic, the kind that sticks to your clothes when you leave.

At the far end of the room, Jason is still telling stories, Alex rolls her eyes but hides a smile, Paul checks his phone though his gaze keeps drifting toward Bella, and Luis laughs from the kitchen counter—his laugh spilling out like sunlight into every corner of the room.

And in the middle of it all, Bella—watching, remembering, and unknowingly becoming the centerpiece of this little mural of youth, affection, and quiet chaos.
